data.description:
# implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when the child's work completed and terminal state was reached

## Headline

`implement.py drive <parent-id>` treats a per-child session **timeout** (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `_default_session_spawner`) as a hard child failure — it stops the whole epic chain and reports `success: false` / `failed_child` — **without reconciling against the child's actual work-item state**. Observed in the WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB epic (three children): each child session was killed at the per-child timeout (3600s/7200s/10800s) **after** the child had already committed and pushed to `dev`, yet `drive` reported:

```
"result": "failed",
"reason": "Child session for WL-0MVGU4S58003IRXV timed out after 3600s."
```

In two of the three cases the child had verifiably reached terminal state (status `completed`/stage `in_review` + commit on `origin/dev`); in the third the work was pushed but the final `StatusLifecycle` terminal update had not yet run, leaving the item stranded `in-progress` (manually finalised afterwards).

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive` (SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) spawns a fresh Pi session per child via `_default_session_spawner`:

- `subprocess.run([pi, "-p", "/skill:implement <child>", "--approve", "--no-extensions"], cwd=worktree, timeout=child_timeout)`.
- On `TimeoutExpired` it returns `{"success": false, "reason": "Child session for <id> timed out after Ns"}`.
- `phase_drive` breaks on any `not spawn_result["success"]`, recording `"result": "failed"` and stopping.

The drive loop never re-queries the child with `wl show` after a timeout to check whether the child actually finished (`status: completed / stage: in_review`, commit on `dev`). `_is_terminal_child` exists and is used by `phase_parent`, but the drive loop decides success purely from the spawned process's exit code/exit-within-timeout, not from the work item's state.

**Observable outcomes (from WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB, implement session herdr-1792524101-1636143-211):**

1. Child work is complete + pushed + item already terminal, but the drive reports the child as failed and stops the chain → operator must manually re-inspect and re-run `parent`.
2. Child killed by the timeout **between push and the final `StatusLifecycle` terminal update** → item left `in-progress` with work on `dev` (an orphaned in-progress that `wl next` filters out); a human/agent must manually finalise the status.
3. No diagnostic distinguishes "completed-late" from "genuinely stuck" — the report only has the generic "timed out after Ns" reason.

## Users

- **herdr downtime dispatcher / producers** driving epics: needs `drive` to complete children reliably and report truthful per-child results.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a `failed` child that is actually `completed`/`in_review` on `dev` is a false negative; the audit trail is wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a driven child's session times out but the child's work item has reached a terminal state (status `completed`/`done` or stage `in_review`) with its commit pushed to `dev`, the drive report does **not** fail that child and does **not** stop the chain: it records the actual terminal status (e.g. result `ok`/`completed-late` with the terminal evidence), continues driving remaining children, and advances the parent when all children are terminal. Unit-testable with a fake spawner that simulates a timeout while `wl show` reports the child as terminal (like `phase_drive`'s existing injectable `spawn_session`/`parent_runner`).
- When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
- The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
- Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the session-per-child isolation and per-child worktree semantics unchanged (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9).
- The reconciliation must be read-only against `wl` (no mutation of a possibly-terminal child's state beyond the existing finalise path); do not re-spawn a session for an already-terminal child (existing "terminal children are never re-implemented" guard).
- Do not change the actual per-child timeout mechanism itself unless the RCA shows it is wrong (the defect is the *consequence handling*, not the timeout).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_default_session_spawner` (line ~5160) — timeout → `success: false`, generic reason.
  - `phase_drive` (line ~5295) — breaks on `not spawn_result["success"]`, no terminal-state reconciliation.
  - `_is_terminal_child` / `_is_terminal_status` (line ~740) — already used by `phase_parent`.
- `examples/` and implement-skill tests cover drive loop, parent advancement, worktree-placement guard; none cover timeout-with-terminal-child reconciliation (per repo search).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `_default_session_spawner`, terminal-state helpers.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend drive-loop tests with a timeout-reconciliation fixture (injectable `spawn_session`).

## Related work

- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 (completed) — implement skill: drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child).
- SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 (completed) — when implementing an epic, start a new session for each child.
- SA-0MUY9PYBD009Y7J5 (completed) — fix Pi turn_end boundary error in driven child sessions (child stderr noise; related child-session reliability).
- WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB (ContextHub epic) — the epic whose three driven children exhibited this in production.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1.** The observed real-world outcomes (false-negative failed report + stranded `in-progress`) are caused by the missing terminal-state reconciliation in `phase_drive` (the only code path consistent with "work pushed + item terminal, yet drive reports timeout failure"). This is the same defect class as the manual finalisation needed for WL-0MVGUA9EY003XFAD.
- **Assumption A2.** A reconciliation pass is preferable to raising the timeout: child sessions do complete; the timeout is a bound (not a verdict). Recommended fix: after a spawn timeout, re-fetch the child's state and classify.
data.title: implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when child completed (no terminal-state reconciliation)

created - Session ID: herdr-1792524101-1636143-211 - /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-10-20T19-21-43-123Z_herdr-1792524101-1636143-211.jsonl

Discovered while driving epic WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB (ContextHub): all three children committed+pushed to dev before their sessions were killed at the per-child timeout, yet drive reported 'timed out after Ns' and failed the chain. Third child (WL-0MVGUA9EY003XFAD) was killed between push and the final StatusLifecycle update — had to finalise its status manually. Root cause is in phase_drive/_default_session_spawner (no terminal-state reconciliation after a spawn timeout).
